response.sql: WITH sex_counts AS (SELECT p.SEX AS sex, COUNT(*) AS test_count FROM Laboratory AS l JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX <> '' OR p.SEX IS NULL GROUP BY p.SEX), totals AS (SELECT AVG(test_count) AS avg_count, SUM(test_count) AS total_count FROM sex_counts) SELECT s.sex, s.test_count, CAST(s.test_count AS REAL) / t.total_count AS fraction_of_total, s.test_count - t.avg_count AS above_average FROM sex_counts AS s CROSS JOIN totals AS t WHERE s.test_count > t.avg_count;

assumptions.assumption: The fraction uses the total test count across all sex groups before the above-average filter.

alternatives.interpretation: The fraction uses only the total test count of sex groups that are above average.
alternatives.sql: WITH sex_counts AS (SELECT p.SEX AS sex, COUNT(*) AS test_count FROM Laboratory AS l JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX <> '' OR p.SEX IS NULL GROUP BY p.SEX), average_count AS (SELECT AVG(test_count) AS avg_count FROM sex_counts), qualifying AS (SELECT s.sex, s.test_count, s.test_count - a.avg_count AS above_average FROM sex_counts AS s CROSS JOIN average_count AS a WHERE s.test_count > a.avg_count) SELECT sex, test_count, CAST(test_count AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(test_count) FROM qualifying) AS fraction_of_total, above_average FROM qualifying;
